sentences.en: Donnie Simpson hosted BET's Video Soul with a tapered number and a silky smoothness that could line a tuxedo jacket.
sentences.zh: 唐尼·辛普森主持黑人娱乐电视台的《灵魂音乐视频》时，留着修剪精致的胡子，其柔顺感甚至能衬托一件燕尾服夹克。

sentences.en: Through a rock at an old jet magazine from the 1980s, you'll hit somebody's mustache.
sentences.zh: 随便朝一本20世纪80年代的旧《Jet》杂志扔块石头，你都能砸中某个人的胡子。

sentences.en: But well before then, the politics of self-presentation had coalesced around grander, less deniable hair.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前很久，自我展示的政治已经凝聚在更宏大、更不容忽视的头发周围。

sentences.en: They migrated to the afro.
sentences.zh: 它们转向了爆炸头。

sentences.en: A mustache might have been a dignified symbol in the pursuit of equality, but there was nothing inherently black about it.
sentences.zh: 在追求平等的过程中，胡子可能是一个尊严的象征，但它并没有什么本质上的黑人属性。

sentences.en: A mustache meant business.
sentences.zh: 胡子意味着动真格。

sentences.en: An afro meant power.
sentences.zh: 爆炸头意味着力量。

sentences.en: I knew before the summer's Black Lives Matter protests that my mustache made me look like a bougie race man.
sentences.zh: 在今夏的“黑人的命也是命”抗议活动之前，我就知道我的胡子让我看起来像个小资黑人精英。

sentences.en: A professional, seemingly humorless, middle-class Negro.
sentences.zh: 一个专业、看似古板的中产阶级黑人。

sentences.en: A moderate who believes that presentation is a crucial component of the advancement part of the NAACP mission.
sentences.zh: 一个温和派，认为外表是 NAACP 使命中促进平权部分至关重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Someone who doesn't mind a little respectability because he believes his people deserve respect.
sentences.zh: 一个不介意体面的人，因为他相信自己的人民理应获得尊重。

sentences.en: It's a look to ponder as the country finds itself churning once again over ceaseless questions of advancement and justice and the right to be left to hell alone.
sentences.zh: 当这个国家再次因关于进步、正义以及要求彻底别来烦我的无休止问题而翻江倒海时，这是一个值得深思的外表。

sentences.en: I live a street over from a thoroughfare where the protests happened almost nightly in June and July.
sentences.zh: 我住的地方离6月和7月几乎每晚都发生抗议活动的大道只有一个街区之隔。

sentences.en: I could hear their approach from my living room.
sentences.zh: 我在客厅里就能听到他们接近的声音。

sentences.en: One evening, I stood at a corner, moved.
sentences.zh: 一天傍晚，我站在街角，深受触动。

sentences.en: As thousands of people passed, friends, colleagues, co-workers, some guy I went on a blind date with a million years ago, chanting, brandishing banners and buttons.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人从我身边走过，有朋友、同事、同行，还有我几百万年前在盲约中见过的某个人，他们高喊着口号，挥舞着横幅和徽章。

sentences.en: Some protesters had their fists raised in a Black power salute.
sentences.zh: 一些抗议者举起拳头，做出黑人力量的敬礼手势。

sentences.en: So I raised mine.
sentences.zh: 于是我举起了手臂。

sentences.en: Not a gesture I would normally make, but there was something about seeing so many white people lifting their arms that goaded me into doing it too.
sentences.zh: 这不是我通常会做的手势，但看到那么多白人都在高举手臂，那种氛围怂恿着我也照做了。

sentences.en: Mine kept lowering itself, so I had to jerk it to its fullest, most committed extension.
sentences.zh: 我的手一直在往下垂，所以我不得不猛地把它伸得最高、最坚定。

sentences.en: I felt out of control, like Edward Norton throwing himself around his boss's office in Fight Club, like the kleptomaniac that
sentences.zh: 我感到失控，就像《搏击俱乐部》里爱德华·诺顿在老板办公室里把自己摔来摔去，就像那个患有盗窃癖的

sentences.en: Tippi Hedren played in Alfred Hitchcock's Marnie, trying to palm a stack of cash, but her arm just won't pick it up.
sentences.zh: 蒂比·海德伦在阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克的《艳贼》中所扮演的角色，试图把一叠现金揣进手心，但她的胳膊就是拿不起来。

sentences.en: At some point, I stopped straining.
sentences.zh: 在某个瞬间，我停止了紧绷。

sentences.en: This wasn't the struggle I came for.
sentences.zh: 这不是我来这里想要经历的挣扎。

sentences.en: Plus, a friend told me later that I had made my fist wrong.
sentences.zh: 另外，后来有个朋友告诉我，我握拳的姿势不对。

sentences.en: The Black power salute is not a casual gesture.
sentences.zh: 黑人力量的致意手势并非一个随意的动作。

sentences.en: It's weaponry.
sentences.zh: 它是武器。

sentences.en: You aim that arm and fire.
sentences.zh: 你瞄准那条手臂然后开火。

sentences.en: I aimed mine in solidarity, with white people instead of at a system they personify.
sentences.zh: 我带着声援的目的举起了手臂，是向白人声援，而不是针对他们所象征的体制。

sentences.en: And that didn't feel quite right.
sentences.zh: 这感觉有点不对劲。

sentences.en: But how would I know?
sentences.zh: 但我怎么会知道呢？

sentences.en: I had never done a Black power salute.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有做过黑人力量的致意手势。

sentences.en: It always seemed like more Blackness than I've needed, maybe more than I had.
sentences.zh: 这似乎总是表现出比我所需要的、甚至比我本身更多的黑人特质。

sentences.en: I'm not Black power black.
sentences.zh: 我并不是那种黑人力量式的黑人。

sentences.en: I've always been milder, more apprehensive than that.
sentences.zh: 我一直以来都更温和、更胆小。

sentences.en: I was practically born with a mustache.
sentences.zh: 我几乎生来就带着小胡子。

sentences.en: I grew up in Philadelphia in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 我在20世纪80年代的费城长大。

sentences.en: My mother left my father when my sister and I was small.
sentences.zh: 在我妹妹和我还小的时候，我母亲就离开了我父亲。

sentences.en: I took the divorce just fine, except for the stealing.
sentences.zh: 除了偷窃这件事，我对父母离异接受得很好。

sentences.en: I used to pluck quarters from my mother's change person before class, feed them to the arcade consoles at the 7-Eleven near school.
sentences.zh: 我过去常常在上课前从母亲的零钱盒里偷拿25美分硬币，塞进学校附近7-Eleven便利店的街机里。

sentences.en: First, though, I would discreetly jam handfuls of one-cent candy into my pockets.
sentences.zh: 不过，在那之前，我会先把一把把一分钱的糖果偷偷塞进口袋。

sentences.en: The quarters were never meant to cover that.
sentences.zh: 那些硬币本来就不是用来付这个钱的。

sentences.en: For two weeks in the second grade, this is how my mornings began, until I got caught.
sentences.zh: 在二年级的两个星期里，我的早晨就是这样开始的，直到我被抓了个现行。

sentences.en: The store manager called my mother, and in the uncomfortably long wait for her arrival, I sat there, wallowing in regret.
sentences.zh: 店经理打电话给我母亲，在漫长得让人难受的等待她到来的过程中，我坐在那里，沉浸在懊悔之中。

sentences.en: But she never showed.
sentences.zh: 但她根本没露面。

sentences.en: My father did.
sentences.zh: 来的是我父亲。

sentences.en: She must have phoned him.
sentences.zh: 她肯定给他打过电话了。

sentences.en: He walked me home to the house he no longer lived in and spanked me, a first for us both.
sentences.zh: 他把我走着带回了他已经不再居住的房子，并狠狠揍了我的屁股，这在我们俩的记忆中都是第一次。

sentences.en: Then he calmly walked me to school.
sentences.zh: 然后他平静地陪着我走到学校。

sentences.en: On the way, he explained, with uncharacteristic gravity, that because I was
sentences.zh: 在路上，他以一种罕有的严肃语气向我解释说，因为我是

sentences.en: Black, I needed to be very careful about my behavior.
sentences.zh: 黑人，所以我必须对自己的行为非常小心。

sentences.en: Nobody should steal, and we especially should.
sentences.zh: 谁都不应该偷窃，而我们尤其不能。

sentences.en: He was a track coach, and that was one of the few times he ever coached me.
sentences.zh: 他是一名田径教练，那是他为数不多对进行我指导的时刻之一。

sentences.en: It's perhaps absurd to point to one childhood incident and declare it decisive, but I've always found that story useful.
sentences.zh: 把童年的某次事件挑出来并断言它是决定性的，或许有些荒谬，但我一直觉得那个故事很有用。

sentences.en: It's rich in disappointment, embarrassment, shame, and guilt.
sentences.zh: 它充满了失望、尴尬、羞耻和内疚。

sentences.en: My mother needed those quarters.
sentences.zh: 我母亲当时很需要那些硬币。

sentences.en: They were car fare, and the kids at school now knew I was a thief.
sentences.zh: 那是车费，而且学校里的孩子们现在都知道我是个小偷了。

sentences.en: I was so ashamed that I vowed at six that I never wanted to feel like that again.
sentences.zh: 我感到如此羞耻，以至于在六岁时就发誓再也不想有这种感觉了。

sentences.en: I'd had a moral near-death experience.
sentences.zh: 我经历了一次道德上的濒死体验。

sentences.en: From there on, I would be good.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我要做一个好孩子。

sentences.en: That was the vow.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的誓言。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 免费解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权。

sentences.en: Good meant trying hard and helping out and listening and being a devoted friend.
sentences.zh: “好”意味着努力尝试、施以援手、倾听以及做一个忠实的朋友。

sentences.en: It meant only the best news for my parents and being liked.
sentences.zh: 这意味着为父母带来最好的消息并讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: But goodness as a personal policy is strange for a child to have.
sentences.zh: 但将“善良”作为个人准则对一个孩子来说是很奇怪的。

sentences.en: It's for grown-ups, not for kids.
sentences.zh: 这是成年人该做的事，而不是小孩子。

sentences.en: Teachers like good kids.
sentences.zh: 老师喜欢乖孩子。

sentences.en: Some teachers prefer them.
sentences.zh: 有些老师更偏爱他们。

sentences.en: The kind of goodness I'm talking about is suspicious to other kids.
sentences.zh: 我所说的这种乖巧，在其他孩子看来是可疑的。

sentences.en: Kids don't want to catch you abstaining from trouble or raising your hand or staying behind after school to help out or, worse, to hang.
sentences.zh: 孩子们可不想看到你克制自己不去惹麻烦、积极举手发言、放学后留下来帮忙，或者更糟糕的是，留下来社交。

sentences.en: I went to the same small, mostly black private school from third grade until graduation.
sentences.zh: 从三年级到毕业，我都就读于同一所规模不大、几乎全都是黑人的私立学校。

sentences.en: That kind of goodness sometimes got classified as white.
sentences.zh: 那种乖巧有时会被归类为白人风格。

sentences.en: It wasn't pejorative, exactly.
sentences.zh: 倒也不是贬义。

sentences.en: Kids liked me.
sentences.zh: 孩子们都很喜欢我。

sentences.en: But we all seemed to realize that now I had a genre.
sentences.zh: 但我们似乎都意识到，现在的我拥有了一种独特的风格定位。

sentences.en: I don't recall making a conscious equation between goodness and whiteness.
sentences.zh: 我不记得自己曾有意识地把乖巧与白人特质划等号。

sentences.en: But I watched TV and went to movies and devoured comic books and music videos in which most of the people were white.
sentences.zh: 但我看过电视、去电影院看过电影，还疯狂阅读漫画书、观看音乐录影带，里面绝大多数人都是白人。

sentences.en: I made identifications.
sentences.zh: 我产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: I internalized things.
sentences.zh: 我将这些东西内化了。

sentences.en: I watched almost every episode of two popular sitcoms in which rich white people adopt black orphans.
sentences.zh: 我几乎看完了两部热门情景喜剧的每一集，剧中的富裕白人都收养了黑人孤儿。

sentences.en: Hip-hop had only begun its pursuit of world domination.
sentences.zh: 嘻哈音乐才刚刚开始它征服世界的步伐。

sentences.en: It was still just rap.
sentences.zh: 它当时还只是说唱。

sentences.en: But I preferred pop music and liked it when a rap song, Push It, Just a Friend, Going Back to Cali, crossed from black radio to everybody else's.
sentences.zh: 但我更喜欢流行音乐，当一首说唱歌曲，比如《Push It》、《Just a Friend》、《Going Back to Cali》，从黑人电台打榜到所有人的电台时，我会很高兴。

sentences.en: The crossing over was validating.
sentences.zh: 这种跨界融合令人感到一种认可。

sentences.en: Pop was proof not of selling out, but of a kind of goodness.
sentences.zh: 流行音乐证明的不是出卖灵魂，而是一种纯粹的美好。

sentences.en: I never suffered any major drama about being black or being gay.
sentences.zh: 我从未因身为黑人或同性恋而经历过什么重大的戏剧性波折。

sentences.en: A stretch of the sixth grade featured me talking like Jack A.
sentences.zh: 六年级有一段时间，我说话的腔调像杰克·A·

sentences.en: Harry, who played the flamboyantly congested sex spot, Sandra, on 227.
sentences.zh: 哈里，他在《227》中饰演了那个风情万种、嗓音沙哑的性感尤物桑德拉。

sentences.en: I just understood that there were strata and somewhere among them were my proper diction and pegged genes.
sentences.zh: 我只是明白，社会存在阶层，而在其中的某个地方，有着我得体的发音和修身的裤子。

sentences.en: I had made myself an individual and was never tortured too terribly for it.
sentences.zh: 我把自己塑造成了一个独立个体，并且没有因此遭受太可怕的折磨。

sentences.en: I had a little room of my own in a wider black world.
sentences.zh: 在更广阔的黑人群体世界里，我有属于自己的一小片天地。

sentences.en: Then Carlton moved in.
sentences.zh: 然后卡尔顿搬了进来。

sentences.zh: 卡尔顿是威尔·史密斯在《新鲜王子妙事多》中富有而保守的表弟。

sentences.en: Bel-Air.
sentences.zh: 贝莱尔。

sentences.en: The show ran on NBC from 1990 to 1996 and was another black adoption sitcom.
sentences.zh: 该剧于1990年至1996年在NBC播出，是又一部黑人收养题材的情景喜剧。

sentences.en: Only the rich family was black.
sentences.zh: 只不过那个富裕的家庭是黑人。

sentences.en: Carlton was the middle kid, bellowingly enunciative, preppy in Ralph Lauren and everything, deafened by the setting on Will's blackness.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿是家里排行居中的孩子，说话字正腔圆声音洪亮，穿着拉尔夫·劳伦等品牌的学院风服装，对威尔的黑人特质的设定感到十分无感。

sentences.en: To Will, Carlton's familiarity with whiteness made him indistinguishable from it.
sentences.zh: 在威尔看来，卡尔顿对白人文化的熟悉让他与白人毫无区别。

sentences.en: Early in season one, when a family friend chooses
sentences.zh: 在第一季初，当一个家族朋友选择

sentences.en: Carlton and not Will to drive his fancy car to Palm Springs as a favor, a miffed Will asks, this is a black thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿而不是威尔开着他那辆豪车去棕榈泉办事时，气恼的威尔质问：这是因为黑人身份，对吧？

sentences.en: On the road, Carlton offers Will a snack.
sentences.zh: 在路上，卡尔顿拿出一份零食给威尔。

sentences.en: What do you say to an Oreo?
sentences.zh: 你怎么称呼奥利奥饼干？

sentences.en: Will answers, what's up, Carlton?
sentences.zh: 威尔回答说，怎么了，卡尔顿？

sentences.en: Carlton's erudition and country club style panic
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿的博学多才和乡村俱乐部风格让

sentences.en: Will, whose own approach to blackness becomes an overcompensation for his proximity to affluence.
sentences.zh: 威尔感到恐慌，他处理自己黑人身份的方式变成了对自己身处富裕阶层的一种过度补偿。

sentences.en: His blackness is a thing he performs, for an audience, but mainly for himself.
sentences.zh: 他的黑人身份是他的一种表演，为了观众，但主要是为了他自己。

sentences.en: In season two,
sentences.zh: 在第二季中，

sentences.en: Uncle Phil tells Will that he's proud of him, that he's just like his son.
sentences.zh: 菲尔叔叔告诉威尔他为他感到骄傲，说他就像自己的亲生儿子一样。

sentences.en: It's a compliment that induces a nervous breakdown.
sentences.zh: 这是一个引发精神崩溃的赞美。

sentences.en: I'm turning into Carlton, Will says.
sentences.zh: 我正在变成卡尔顿，威尔说道。

sentences.en: No more of these sissy sandwiches, no more valet parking, and no more of these preppy parties, man.
sentences.zh: 再也没有这些娘娘腔的三明治了，再也没有代客泊车了，也再没有这些学院风派对了好吗，老兄。

sentences.en: He then destroys the
sentences.zh: 随后他毁掉了那张

sentences.en: $200 check that he kissed up to Uncle Phil to write him and says, yo, the funky fresh is back in the flesh with a vengeance, Holmes.
sentences.zh: 200美元的支票，那是他为了让菲尔叔叔开给她而阿谀奉承得来的，并说道：嘿，那个时髦带劲的硬汉又卷土重来了，老兄。

sentences.en: It's stunning enough, the equation of intelligence with emasculation and whiteness with lunch, Will sandwiches.
sentences.zh: 将知识等同于阉割，将白人特质等同于午餐和威尔的三明治，这已经足够让人大跌眼镜了。

sentences.en: But when he's finished, the audience erupts in cheers.
sentences.zh: 但当他说完时，观众席爆发出一阵欢呼。

sentences.en: Nobody watching wanted Will to become good.
sentences.zh: 观看节目的所有人都不希望威尔变好。

sentences.en: They wanted him to stay black.
sentences.zh: 他们希望他保持黑人本色。

sentences.en: I didn't know who Carlton was until I was presumed to be him.
sentences.zh: 我以前并不知道卡尔顿是谁，直到我被别人认定我就是他。

sentences.en: In school, at my weekend movie theater job, in the checkout line at the gap.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，在我周末的电影院工作岗位上，在Gap服装店的结账队伍里。

sentences.en: He equipped the young and perplexed with a shorthand for bright, square oddballs who weren't quite nerds.
sentences.zh: 他为那些年轻而困惑的人提供了一个代名词，用来指代那些聪明、古板、有些怪异却又不算真正的书呆子的人。

sentences.en: Nerds were easy.
sentences.zh: 书呆子很好归类。

sentences.en: They were Steve Urkel, the geek from Family Matters.

sentences.en: In high school, there were a few of us oddballs.

sentences.zh: 这是男性青春期的经典仪式。

sentences.zh: 我留胡子是因为我能留，留着是因为它没违反着装规范，我很感激它，因为它可能帮我压制了那些同性恋恐惧者。

sentences.en: Just about every boy in my graduating class had something sprouting above their lip, wispy, ghostly, cheesy, but certifiably masculine.

sentences.en: That's also why people called me Carlton, because I bore the vaguest resemblance to Alfonso Ribeiro, the actor who played him.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么人们叫我卡尔顿，因为我和阿方索·里贝罗——那个扮演他的演员——有着极其微弱的相似之处。

sentences.en: We both talked funny, dressed funny, danced funny, and we both, it must be said, had a mustache.
sentences.zh: 我们说话滑稽、穿着滑稽、跳舞滑稽，而且必须承认，我们都留着小胡子。

sentences.en: On my way to college, I got rid of it, hoping to exercise Carlton, and it didn't go with the look I wanted to take with me.
sentences.zh: 在去大学的路上，我把它剃了，希望能甩掉卡尔顿的影子，而且它也与我想带去的造型不搭。

sentences.en: It was a week of sitting around, exploiting the pretext of food and talent shows to luxuriate in the personalities and tastes and lives of potential new friends.
sentences.zh: 那是一个坐在一起度过的星期，借着食物和才艺秀的幌子，沉浸在潜在新朋友的个性、品味和生活中。

sentences.en: It was exciting finding these kindred souls.
sentences.zh: 找到这些志同道合的灵魂真是令人兴奋。

sentences.zh: 每隔一段时间，我们中的某个人就会暂停我们的小天堂，为这一切的荒谬大笑一番。

sentences.zh: 我并没有把生活中的人仅仅当作白人来看待。

sentences.en: These were my co-workers, my friends.
sentences.zh: 这些是我的同事，我的朋友。

sentences.en: One of those friends applied a similar logic to me.
sentences.zh: 其中一位朋友对我也应用了类似的逻辑。

sentences.en: The same week that a Minneapolis police officer killed Philando Castile, he found me in grief, and I told him that I've always harbored a murmuring awareness that I could be shot.
sentences.zh: 就在明尼阿波利斯一名警察杀害菲兰多·卡斯蒂尔的同一周，他在我悲伤时找到了我，我告诉他，我内心一直隐隐意识到自己也可能被枪杀。

sentences.en: He was incredulous.
sentences.zh: 他对此难以置信。

sentences.en: How could that happen to me?
sentences.zh: 这种事怎么会发生在我身上？

sentences.en: I went to a good school and had a good job.
sentences.zh: 我上了好学校，有着好工作。

sentences.en: I was black, but not killed during a police stop black.
sentences.zh: 我是黑人，但不是那种会在警察拦截盘查时被杀的黑人。

sentences.en: I was good.
sentences.zh: 我是个好人。

sentences.en: I can imagine a version of myself that, having completed Yale and succeeded professionally, would have heard that response and felt relieved.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象另一个版本的自己，在完成耶鲁学业并获得职业成功后，听到那样的回应会感到宽慰。

sentences.en: That I was one of racism's carve-outs.
sentences.zh: 庆幸自己是种族主义豁免的特例。

sentences.en: I was me.
sentences.zh: 我就是我。

sentences.en: Only, I've always felt more lucky than exceptional.
sentences.zh: 只是，我一直觉得自己是幸运，而非出众。

sentences.en: I can now see that my vow of goodness was an existential shift of shape.
sentences.zh: 我现在能看出，我成为“好人”的誓言其实是一种生存状态的变形。

sentences.en: Having been told early on that unreasonable obstacles awaited, I set about finding a form that could easily evade them.
sentences.zh: 由于早早就被告知前方有无数不合理的障碍，我开始寻找一种能够轻松避开它们的形态。

sentences.en: There is, I suppose, another hand, wherein I take further stock and declare a folly.
sentences.zh: 我想，还有另一种可能，那就是我重新审视并宣布那是一种愚蠢。

sentences.en: The entire affair of race is a joke.
sentences.zh: 种族这整件事就是一个笑话。

sentences.en: My life is mine.
sentences.zh: 我的生活属于我自己。

sentences.en: No strings, no speed traps.
sentences.zh: 没有羁绊，没有测速陷阱。

sentences.en: Why overthink it?

sentences.zh: 拜托。

sentences.zh: 这叫大流行时期的潮流。

sentences.zh: 我在脸上烤了面包。

sentences.zh: 一个人的种族并不等于他自己。

sentences.en: I know this and strive to leave it at that.

sentences.zh: 但我从来走不远。

sentences.en: In the United States, a black self eventually discovers his race is a form of credit or discredit, as it were.

sentences.en: You can't leave home without it.
sentences.zh: 你出门可少不了它。

sentences.en: Yet for as long as black Americans have been conscious of their blackness.
sentences.zh: 然而，只要美国黑人对自己的黑人身份有所觉醒，

sentences.en: Some public intellectual has cried, hoax.
sentences.zh: 总会有某些公共知识分子大喊骗局。

sentences.zh: 自由地做一个普通人。

sentences.zh: 你可以让自己被提飞升。

sentences.zh: 美国文学中专门为那些密谋逃离的角色保留了一个角落。

sentences.zh: 也就是“融入小说”，黑人在其中勉强维持着悲惨的白人生活。

sentences.zh: 离开的逻辑确实存在。

sentences.en: I must admit I do feel free, often in precisely the way that a friend of mine insisted I must, because my fears haven't yet come true.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我的确感到自由，这往往正如我的一位朋友坚持认为的那样，因为我的恐惧尚未成真。

sentences.zh: 理论上，我可以加入黑人退出运动并离开。

sentences.en: I've tried to empathize with this thinking, and I'm always surprised that I can't close the deal.

sentences.en: Lately, and most cantankerously, it's Kanye West who has been daring to level with us.
sentences.zh: 最近，而且是最具抬杠意味的是，坎耶·韦斯特一直敢于对我们直言不讳。

sentences.en: His early musical pushes against black orthodoxy have mutated over the last four years into pleas for black people to stop it with the racism talk, to get over it, essentially.
sentences.zh: 他在早期音乐中对黑人正统观念的反抗，在过去四年里已经演变成恳求黑人停止谈论种族主义，本质上就是看开点。

sentences.en: His vision for transcendence of racism, if not race itself, would be easier to share if it didn't appear to lead straight into the arms of racists.
sentences.zh: 他关于超越种族主义乃至超越种族本身的愿景，如果不是看起来直接把人领进种族主义者的怀抱的话，本会更容易让人接受。

sentences.en: I don't believe in that kind of transcendence.
sentences.zh: 我不相信那种超越。

sentences.en: I'm not a blexiteer, some person who is still convinced that we live in post-racial times.
sentences.zh: 我不是黑人退出论者，不是那种仍然坚信我们生活在后种族时代的人。

sentences.en: If anything,
sentences.zh: 如果要说的话，

sentences.en: I'm a blexistentialiSt. I encounter something like Barack Obama's Dreams from My Father,
sentences.zh: 我是一个黑人存在主义者。我读到巴拉克·奥巴马的《我父亲的梦想》之类的作品，

sentences.en: which is steadfastly the opposite of the passing experience, and feast on his decades-long search for a black self that suits him.
sentences.zh: 这绝对与融入白人社会的经验相反，我如饥似渴地阅读他几十年来寻找适合自己的黑人自我的历程。

sentences.en: It's a finding book, a story of becoming.
sentences.zh: 这是一本寻找自我的书，一部成长的故事。

sentences.en: As the black tent expands, the people beneath it can keep doing as they've always done, widening its poles.
sentences.zh: 随着黑人阵营的扩大，身处其中的人可以继续做他们一直以来在做的事，把帐篷撑得更宽。

sentences.en: I have wondered, though, what kind of spiral I would have taken had the friend on that video call not said, NAACP lawyer, if she had looked at my face and said,
sentences.zh: 不过，我曾想过，如果视频通话中的那个朋友没有说“NAACP律师”，如果她看着我的脸说，

sentences.en: you look like Clarence Thomas, or Herman Cain, or Ben Carson.
sentences.zh: 你看起来像克拉伦斯·托马斯，或者赫尔曼·凯恩，或者本·卡森，我会陷入什么样的漩涡。

sentences.en: Carson's goatee has, on occasion, been only a mustache.
sentences.zh: 卡森的山羊胡有时也仅仅是一撇小胡子。

sentences.en: What if she had pinned me to a bootstraps mentality that rejects racism as a root of injustice, that believes you're your own responsibility?
sentences.zh: 如果她把那种“白手起家”的心态强加给我，而这种心态拒绝将种族主义视为不公正的根源、认为你得为自己负责呢？

sentences.en: I would have felt cornered, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想我会觉得走投无路吧。

sentences.en: Personal accountability isn't nothing.
sentences.zh: 个人问责并非无足轻重。

sentences.en: This country just won't let it be all.
sentences.zh: 只是这个国家不让它成为全部。

sentences.en: The extant number of black firsts, rares, onlys, nevers, not yets, and not quites attests to that, as does the chronic too manys, too oftens, and too soons.
sentences.zh: 历数不尽的黑人第一、罕见、唯一、绝无仅有、前所未有和尚未达到，以及那些长期以来为数过多、过于频繁和过早发生的现象，都证明了这一点。

sentences.en: I like to think that I would have absorbed her Clarence Thomas and regaled her with a separate lineage.
sentences.zh: 我愿意认为，我会接受她把我比作克拉伦斯·托马斯，并向她讲述另一个家族血统。

sentences.en: I would have told her that I hail from a long line of family mustaches.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉她，我出身于一个世代留小胡子的家族。

sentences.en: Uncle Gene's made him look famous.
sentences.zh: 吉恩叔叔的小胡子让他看起来很有名望。

sentences.en: Uncle Jack's got bushy after World War II and pretty much stayed that way.
sentences.zh: 杰克叔叔的小胡子在二战后变得浓密，并且基本上一直保持那样。

sentences.en: My grandmother's last husband, Jimmy, wore his in a style best described as sharpened.
sentences.zh: 我祖母的最后一任丈夫吉米，他的胡子留成了一种最好用“犀利”来形容的风格。

sentences.zh: 她是怎么亲吻那种东西而不需要缝针的？

sentences.zh: 她的第一任丈夫，也就是我的外祖父，留的胡子几乎看不出来。

sentences.en: Both their sons had one.
sentences.zh: 他们的两个儿子每人都留了一撇。

sentences.en: Her brother, Marcellus, liked his thin.
sentences.zh: 她的哥哥马塞勒斯喜欢留细细的胡子。

sentences.en: My mother liked my stepfather's because, well, she loved him.
sentences.zh: 我母亲喜欢我继父的胡子，因为，嗯，她深爱着他。

sentences.en: My father had his faces.
sentences.zh: 我父亲则留过各种样式的胡子。

sentences.en: Three of his brothers had them too.
sentences.zh: 他的三个兄弟也留过。

sentences.en: The fourth, Uncle Bill, had an ascot.
sentences.zh: 老四比尔叔叔则系一条阿斯科特领巾。

sentences.en: Had you ever met Uncle
sentences.zh: 如果你曾见过比尔

sentences.en: Bill, you would conclude that the ascot essentially was a mustache.
sentences.zh: 叔叔，你就会断定那条领巾本质上就是一撇小胡子。

sentences.en: It might just have been simpler to say who didn't have one than who did.
sentences.zh: 与其说谁留了胡子，倒不如说谁没留，这样可能更简单些。

sentences.en: I don't know what everybody's politics were, but as a clan, we were a Thanksgiving spread.
sentences.zh: 我不知道大家的政治立场如何，但作为一个家族，我们就像是一桌感恩节大餐。

sentences.en: A little of everything, yet nothing so outrageous that the advancement for colored people would ever be off the table.
sentences.zh: 什么都有那么一点，却又没有什么过于离谱，以至于让有色人种进阶协进会觉得无法接受。

sentences.en: These were working men, providers, not activists, but voters, certainly.
sentences.zh: 这些人都是劳工，是顶梁柱，谈不上是什么激进分子，但绝对是选民。

sentences.en: Their mustaches strike me now as a generational phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，他们的小胡子似乎是一种代际现象。

sentences.en: These people were all born between 1920 and 1950.
sentences.zh: 这些人全部出生于1920年至1950年之间。

sentences.en: Of their children, only my cousins, Butchie and Kyle, are describable as mustache men.
sentences.zh: 在他们的孩子当中，只有我的表兄弟布奇和凯尔可以算作是留胡子的人。

sentences.en: This is why I've kept mine.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我也留着胡子。

sentences.en: It's me squeezing my way into a parallel heritage.
sentences.zh: 这就像是我在努力挤进一种平行的传承之中。

sentences.en: In this small sense, the work I do caring for it feels connected to a legacy of people who did and do the work chipping at and thinking with this nation.
sentences.zh: 从这个微小的意义上说，我精心打理胡子的工作，让我觉得与这样一群人血脉相连——他们过去和现在都在为这个国家添砖加瓦、深思熟虑。

sentences.en: The good work.
sentences.zh: 那是崇高的事业。

sentences.en: Something obvious in just about any photograph taken of Black Americans during the Civil Rights era is how put together everyone is.
sentences.zh: 在民权运动时期拍摄的几乎任何一张黑人照片中，最显而易见的一点就是每个人都打扮得一丝不苟。

sentences.en: They wore to war what they wore to church.
sentences.zh: 他们去上战场穿的衣服和去教堂穿的一模一样。

sentences.en: The country was watching.
sentences.zh: 整个国家都在看着。

sentences.en: People got dressed up to withstand being put down.
sentences.zh: 人们盛装打扮，以此经受住受到的贬低。

sentences.en: They dressed with full awareness that an outfit risked ruin.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着盛装，心里十分清楚衣服随时可能会被毁掉。

sentences.zh: 裙子被扯得变了形。

sentences.zh: 眼镜碎了。

sentences.zh: 鲜血。

sentences.zh: 哪双好皮鞋没有面临毁灭的风险？

sentences.zh: 它既不能被人一把抓住，也不能被人猛力拽掉。

sentences.en: For as delighted as I am by the sound of the scraping of the blade against my skin, some doubt never fails to creep into the mustache stage.

sentences.zh: 我曾梦见自己失去了它。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
